Carrier cleared by the `domain:ui` seat (`session_01UzHd6hDYatoDn17BuwKxnZ`). `needs:contract-review` stripped here as the third of three carriers in one stroke — PR objectui#9115, card objectui#7334, and this card — on the PASS record at objectui#9115 comment `5630163403`, judged head `066c43e`. ⛔ Stripped because a review record exists and passed, ⛔ not because the label was inconvenient.

⚠️ Why this card carried the label at all, since it is worth knowing for next time: adding `Closes #9114` to PR objectui#9115 made that PR deliver **two** cards, and `check-clause2-carriers --pair 9115` then reported **exit 4** on a C1 split — hung on the PR and on objectui#7334, but not here. The gate is a **dual** carrier, and the second carrier is the only machine-readable evidence that a review was **CLEARED** rather than **STRIPPED**, so the split was closed by hanging it here too, additively, then clearing all three together. ⇒ **a PR that closes a second card owes that card a carrier as well.**

## ⚠️ One correction to this card's own body, recorded before it closes

This card's Remedy space says:

> `ObjectGantt` supplies an `onNavigate` of its own the way `ObjectGrid` and `ObjectCalendar` already do (they are the two of eight view renderers that pass one).

⛔ **`ObjectCalendar` does not.** Verified at source on `origin/main`:

```
plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx:110   onNavigate?: (date: Date) => void;
```

That is a **calendar date-navigation prop** — a different symbol that happens to share a spelling — and it never reaches `useNavigationOverlay`; the calendar's hook call passes `navigation` / `objectName` / `onRowClick` only, exactly as the gantt's did. ⭐ `ObjectGrid` is the **only** one of the eight, and it reads `schema.onNavigate`, a non-author programmatic channel that the schema rejects by name — so copying that spelling into `ObjectGantt` would have left the dead click exactly as it was.

⇒ option 1 was still the right shape, but it could not be satisfied by imitation; it needed a real in-component sink, which is what PR objectui#9115's second leg builds.

⭐ Recorded because the reviewing seat repeated this same error independently, using that `onNavigate` count as a **lit control** in the hold comment — and the dev caught it. A control that lights for the wrong reason is worse than one that stays dark: darkness invites a re-measurement, a false light does not. The full correction is at objectui#9115 comment `5630155580`.

This card closes when objectui#9115 lands.
